Arteta has revived that tradition since he took over in December 2019, recording 1-0 victories32 times in the Premier League, more than any club apart from Everton.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIsak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an endRead moreArsenal scored their first set-piece goal of the season ina routine 2-0 winat home to Everton last Saturday and targeting Liverpool’s weakness from set plays while keeping things tight at the other end could be the most effective tactic against a team who have been finding their feet under Iraola in recent weeks.“Collectively, we acknowledge the importance of defending,” said Arteta last year when asked about comparisons between his team and Graham’s. “We know that if we excel in that part of the game, the chances and the probabilities to win more matches is going to be very, very high.”Arsenal flew back to London after losing to Fleetwood on penalties in a shootout that will have revived bad memories of May’sChampions League final defeat by Paris Saint-Germain.The Carabao Cup has stretched Arteta’s squad in the past two seasons, when they reached first the semi-finals then the final, so that is one potential positive from their elimination – not that the ultra-competitive Spaniard would agree. For him, the only way to respond to the most embarrassing night of his managerial career will be to follow in Graham’s footsteps on Sunday.Explore more on these topicsArsenalLiverpoolfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: NCAA basketball 2026-27 predictions: from JuJu Watkins to Tyran Stokes, the names you’ll know by March | College basketball | The Guardian
description: Can Florida’s continuity trump the transfer portal? Will JuJu Watkins come back strong? And who will survive an expanded March Madness? Our writers weigh in
Author: Ella Brockway
Headline: Can Florida’s continuity trump the transfer portal? Will JuJu Watkins come back strong? And who will survive an expanded March Madness? Our writers weigh in
Content: Notre Dame’s Hannah Hidalgo, Florida’s Thomas Haugh, UConn’s Sarah Strong and Kansas’s Tyran Stokes (from left) are among the biggest names to watch in the new college basketball season.Composite: Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenNotre Dame’s Hannah Hidalgo, Florida’s Thomas Haugh, UConn’s Sarah Strong and Kansas’s Tyran Stokes (from left) are among the biggest names to watch in the new college basketball season.Composite: Getty ImagesCollege basketballNCAA basketball 2026-27 predictions: from JuJu Watkins to Tyran Stokes, the names you’ll know by MarchCan Florida’s continuity trump the transfer portal? Will JuJu Watkins pick up where she left off? And who will survive an expanded March Madness? Our writers weigh inElla Brockway,Bryan Armen Graham,Stephanie KaloiandNicholas LevineFri 30 Oct 2026 07.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 30 Oct 2026 07.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleWhat are you most looking forward to, on or off the court?Lots of stuff.The return ofJuJu Watkinsat USC afterher 19-month injury layoff, the debut of Tyran Stokes at Kansas, the potential turnaround of the Big East on the men’s side, and the stacked ACC on the women’s side.Ella BrockwayJuJu Watkins’ return from injury, obviously, but also the question of whether college hoops can maintain any sense of continuity in the transfer portal era. Michiganwon the men’s nattyin April, thenlost their coach to the NBAand watched much of their roster disintegrate. Florida, meanwhile, have managed to keep the majority of the core fromtheir 2025 title teamtogether. Which model wins out?Bryan Armen GrahamMultiple things, but top of mind: Like many fans of women’s college basketball, I’m already excited by whatJuJu Watkinshas shown in the preseason. She’s been away from the court for a long time, and it will be thrilling to see the presumptive No 1 draft pick take over again.Stephanie KaloiThe new-look Pac-12 Conference.This nine-team league has only two schools that were previously in the Pac-12 and adds five schools from the Mountain West, plus powerhouse Gonzaga from the WCC and Texas State from the Sun Belt. An interesting mix of playing styles, from one of the nation’s best defenses in San Diego State to one of the most efficient offenses year in and year out in Gonzaga.Nicholas LevineThe new 76-team format for men’s and women’s March Madness is …… not good nor necessary nor something that I think will affect most people’s consumption of March Madness.If the tournament is going to expand, I think we should full-send it and go to 128 with first-round games on campus.EB… a solution in search of a problem.When the deadline for most office pools is still Thursday at 12pm Eastern, the games on Tuesday and Wednesday have always felt like the tournament’s waiting room. Now we’re just making that waiting room bigger.BAGView image in fullscreenUSC star JuJu Watkins returns to the court after a long injury layoff as one of the leading contenders for national player of the year honors.Photograph: Jayne Kamin-Oncea/Getty Images… potentially cool!I’m cautiously optimistic that this is more than just another money grab for theNCAA. Hopefully, it means more surprise wins from underdog programs that might not otherwise get a shot at the tournament.SK… fine.Like most people, I’m a “64 just feels so clean and right” guy. I like seeing more quality teams get a chance to compete, but expansion also hurts more of the lower-seeded automatic qualifiers, who now have to play in the First 12 on Tuesday and Wednesday.NLThe surprise package of the season will be …TheMiami menwon 26 games last season but were knocked out in the second round of the tournament. With 6ft 9in forward Malik Reneau back for a fifth year, they’re a top-10 team and a Final Four contender. I’m also excited about Jasmine Bascoe, one of the best point guards in the country last season, running it back for year three with the Villanova women.EBTheMichigan womenhave never reached a Final Four, but they return their top six scorers from an Elite Eight team. Olivia Olson, Syla Swords and Mila Holloway have grown up together and the Big Ten could be there for the taking with defending champions UCLA in a rebuild.BAGI think theMichigan womenwill make more noise than they have in recent years. They finished third in their conference last season, and beyond the usual suspects like South Carolina and UConn, the women’s game feels less predictable than it has in some time.SKTheArizona State men.Randy Bennett spent 25 seasons building Saint Mary’s into one of the country’s most consistent programs, winning 20-plus games 19 times and reaching 12 NCAA Tournaments. An early adopter of the ball-screen-heavy offense now commonplace across the sport, Bennett brings his tactical acumen and attention to detail to a Sun Devils roster loaded with size and skill. Look for ASU to shake up the Big 12.NLView image in fullscreenMichigan State coach Tom Izzo and guard Jeremy Fears Jr look on during the second half of the Spartans’ Sweet 16 matchup with UConn in Washington DC last March.Photograph: Patrick Smith/Getty ImagesWhich team in either preseason top 10 will struggle?In a world where 76 (seventy-six!) teams make the NCAA Tournament, all of these teams should be safe. For the sake of the exercise, I’ll pick theTennessee men. Of the top teams in the SEC, they probably have the lowest possible floor.EBTheMichigan menlost four starters, coach Dusty May to the NBA’s Mavericks and blue-chip recruit Brandon McCoyto a season-ending knee injury. Elliot Cadeau and Trey McKenney give them an elite backcourt, but expecting the Wolverines to remain among the top flight of contenders after so much upheaval feels optimistic.BAGTheNotre Dame womenare in an interesting position. Missing the tournament entirely feels like a stretch, but they’re relying on a lot of young talent this season. UCLA are also rebuilding after losing several seniors to graduation, though the defending champions have earned some breathing room as they put together their next contender.SKTexas Tech men.There is no one in the country more reliant on their fifth-year players remaining eligible than the Red Raiders. If they don’t go three-for-three in their eligibility lawsuits, they simply won’t have enough talent to earn a high seed in the NCAA Tournament.NLThe men’s national player of the year will be …Jeremy Fears Jr, Michigan State. Last season’s national assists leader takes a step up – and maybe even takes the Spartans to their first Final Four since 2019.EBThomas Haugh, Florida. The 6ft 9in forward could already be earning an NBA paycheck, but instead he’s back in Gainesville alongside Alex Condon and Rueben Chinyelu. His versatility and experience make him the centerpiece of a team with legitimate title ambitions.BAGView image in fullscreenMichigan’s Olivia Olson, Mila Holloway and Syla Swords take the court against Oakland in Ann Arbor last December. The Wolverines enter the new season hoping to build on their third-place Big Ten finishPhotograph: Jaime Crawford/Getty ImagesThomas Haugh, Florida.He’s a player I’m watching closely. Passing up strong NBA draft prospects to stick with the program is already a compelling storyline.SKDavid Mirković, Illinois.The 6ft 9in forward from Montenegro suffered a foot injury over the summer and has yet to be cleared to play. Once healthy, the skilled big man will be the best player on one of the best teams in the country. Coach Brad Underwood gives his players the freedom to play to their strengths, and Mirković should be highly productive on both ends of the court.NLThe women’s national player of the year will be …JuJu Watkins, USC.The four-way race between Watkins, Sarah Strong, Hannah Hidalgo and Mikayla Blakes will be the highlight of the season. I’m picking JuJu.EBSarah Strong, UConn.With Azzi Fuddhaving moved on to the WNBA, the reigning national player of the year becomes the undisputed centerpiece of Geno Auriemma’s offense. Strong’s cocktail of scoring, rebounding, passing and defensive instincts is almost unfair. Watkins will generate more headlines, but Strong could put together the more complete season.BAGJuJu Watkins, USC.Sarah Strong is a close second, and I think we’ll see these two battle it out all season. Vanderbilt’s Mikayla Blakes is another to keep an eye on.SKJuju Watkins, USC.Not only could the consensus 2024-25 All-American win national player of the year honors, but she could go down as one of the greatest college players of all time. If her supporting cast can take some of the offensive pressure off her, look for Watkins to lead the Trojans on a deep tournament run.NLView image in fullscreenKansas freshman Tyran Stokes goes up for a lay-up against Louisville during an exhibition game in Lawrence. The highly touted forward is among the leading contenders to be the No 1 pick in next year’s NBA draft.Photograph: Jamie Squire/Getty ImagesThe hottest NBA prospect is …Tyran Stokes, Kansas.The 6ft 7in freshman is the front-runner among the standout freshman prospects. On the older end, Motiejus Krivas could boost himself into the top-five pick conversation with another year at Arizona.EBTyran Stokes, Kansas.He looks like he was designed in a lab for maximum appeal to professional scouts: explosive, versatile, capable of creating his own shot and jumping out of the gym. His jump shot and decision-making remain works in progress, but the physical tools appear to have no ceiling.BAGEveryone is very excited aboutTyran Stokes at Kansas, so I’ll hop on the bandwagon. But he’s got a lot to learn in just a handful of months. Caleb Holt is another dynamic player who should cause a ruckus at Arizona this season.SKTyran Stokes, Kansas.The best high school player in the country last season should follow in Darryn Peterson’s footsteps as a one-and-done Jayhawk. The 6ft 7in wing has an NBA-ready body and the athleticism to guard almost any position. Early signs suggest he can get into the paint and be productive once he’s there. If he continues to develop his perimeter game, he could be the first player taken in the 2027 NBA draft.NLThe hottest WNBA prospect is …Watkins will go No 1 in 2027, but the No 2 pick should beMadison Booker of Texas. The pro scouts will be watching to see what jump her already well-rounded game can take.EBHannah Hidalgo, Notre Dame.At 5ft 6in, she defies the prototype of a modern professional guard. But few players in the country can match her combination of scoring, defensive disruption and sheer competitive motor. The question is whether her diminutive frame limits her professional prospects. I’m betting her talent and tenacity win out.BAGView image in fullscreenUConn’s Sarah Strong grabs a rebound in front of Notre Dame’s Hannah Hidalgo during a January meeting in Storrs. Both return this season among the leading contenders for national player of the year honors.Photograph: Joe Buglewicz/Getty ImagesI’m going to stick withJuJu Watkins, but Madison Booker cannot and should not be ignored. Ultimately, this may come down to what each team needs most.SKJuJu Watkins, USC.She appears to be a no-brainer as the best WNBA prospect. Not only does she have great size and athleticism, but she also checks the “smart, tough, skilled” boxes all coaches are looking for.NLOne bold predictionThe expanded tournament won’t generate much of a reaction.Expansion is the way of the future, from the World Cup to tennis majors to leagues themselves, because more teams means more games means more money. This year’s tournaments will probably feel bloated and include a few more lopsided results, but I suspect most fans will either begrudgingly enjoy an extra upset or two – or just skip the play-in round entirely and tune in starting Thursday.EBRick Pitino takes St John’s to the Final Four.The Red Storm have won 61 games and two Big East tournament titles over the past two seasons, but haven’t advanced beyond the Sweet 16. With a formidable NIL war chest and a 74-year-old Hall of Fame coach who cannot go on forever, the urgency is palpable. This is the year Pitino delivers the program’s first Final Four appearance since 1985 – an outcome that suddenly feels natural with theLibertyandKnickshaving primed the pump by ending decades-long droughts of their own in recent years.BAGAfter an OK first season and an absolutely brutal second under head coach Kim Caldwell, I thinkTennessee’s women will surprise a lot of people. They’ve brought in a strong, enthusiastic group, and there’s something powerful about rebuilding a roster from scratch. Caldwell is such a unique force in college basketball. I think they’ll make a serious push come tournament time.SKThe New Mexico men win the new-look Mountain West and make a tournament run.Eric Olen is in his second year in Albuquerque and has retained All-Mountain West first-teamer Jake Hall, the preseason conference player of the year, along with backcourt partner Uriah Tenette. The Lobos have also added a mix of European pros and transfers. The last time Olen had this much skill and positional size, he led UC San Diego to 31 wins and an NCAA tournament appearance. Grand Canyon will provide the stiffest competition in the conference, but look for Olen and the Lobos not only to secure the automatic bid but also to reach the Sweet 16.NLView image in fullscreenDuke’s bench react during an exhibition game against Tennessee at Cameron Indoor Stadium. The Blue Devils enter the new season among the favorites for the men’s national championship after two consecutive March Madness disappointments.Photograph: Jared C Tilton/Getty ImagesMen’s Final FourArizona, Duke, Florida, Illinois.EBArizona, Florida, Illinois, St John’s.BAGDuke, Florida, Michigan, UConn.SKArizona, Illinois, Louisville, Michigan State.NLMen’s national championDuke. I’ve spent too much of my life watching the Blue Devils (albeit from the other side of the Tobacco Road rivalry) to believe they’ll let a third straight NCAA Tournament heartbreak happen. They have a deep roster, but their biggest threats will be from Florida and Illinois, who also spent the offseason retaining and retooling.EBFlorida.In a sport increasingly defined by roster turnover, Todd Golden has achieved something remarkable: keeping much of his 2025 championship core together. Haugh, Condon and Chinyelu give the Gators the kind of experienced, physically imposing frontcourt that grinds out wins in March. Duke may have more individual talent, but the Gators have something harder to manufacture: continuity.BAGUConn.That loss to the Wolverines was a tough pill to swallow, and I expect they’ll come back laser-focused on getting the biggest win of all this season. There’s plenty of motivation to go one better.SKIllinois.The Fighting Illini have experienced returners who are proven winners. With an international-heavy roster and great size and skill at every position, they’re a matchup nightmare for opponents. At one point last season, they had the highest offensive efficiency rating of the KenPom era. The health of David Mirković and Andrej Stojaković will be critical, but their combination of skill and winning experience gives them the edge over powers like Duke and Florida for me.NLWomen’s Final FourNotre Dame, South Carolina, UConn, USC.EBMichigan, South Carolina, UConn, USC.BAGMichigan, South Carolina, UConn, USC.SKLSU, South Carolina, UConn, USC.NLWomen’s national championSouth Carolinawereembarrassed in the national title gameagainst UCLA last season. Dawn Staley and co will use that as fuel. The Gamecocks have a gauntlet of a schedule, but they also have valuable depth that will pay off in November and in March.EBSouth Carolina. Dawn Staley has enough frontcourt talent to field two formidable teams, with Joyce Edwards, Chloe Kitts and Ashlyn Watkins headlining an embarrassment of riches. Add Tessa Johnson’s experience and a promising collection of newcomers and the Gamecocks look built to withstand just about anything. Last April’s title-game humiliation against UCLA should provide all the motivation they need.BAGSouth Carolina, probably, and I’m making my peace with it, despite always enjoying the possibility of a surprise. Dawn Staley continues to build teams that are light years ahead of the rest. And after losing last season’s championship, I suppose the Gamecocks are underdogs in a way. Their talented freshmen should fit in nicely alongside the veterans.SKUSC.I’m sticking with the JuJu theme and predicting she’ll lead the Trojans past their crosstown rivals UCLA. The generational star will most likely turn pro after this season, but not before cutting down the nets in Columbus.NLExplore more on these topicsCollege basketballCollege sportsUS sportsNCAA TournamentNCAAfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Fiesta awaits in Mexico City as Kimi Antonelli speeds towards F1 history | Formula One 2026 | The Guardian
description: Italian 20-year-old is on the verge of becoming the youngest world champion with Mexico City ready for a carnival coronation atmosphere
Author: Giles Richards
Headline: Italian 20-year-old is on the verge of becoming the youngest world champion with Mexico City ready for a carnival coronation atmosphere
Content: Kimi Antonelli will have no shortage of support from the fans in Mexico as he closes in on his first title.Photograph: Manuel Velasquez/Formula 1/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenKimi Antonelli will have no shortage of support from the fans in Mexico as he closes in on his first title.Photograph: Manuel Velasquez/Formula 1/Getty ImagesFormula One 2026Fiesta awaits in Mexico City as Kimi Antonelli speeds towards F1 historyItalian 20-year-old is on the verge of becoming the youngest world champion with the Mexican Grand Prix ready for a carnival coronation atmosphereGiles Richardsin Mexico CityFri 30 Oct 2026 16.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 30 Oct 2026 19.25 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAn undeniable highlight of this Formula One season, marked by discontent at the new regulations, has been getting swept along by the sheer joy that the world champion-in-waiting,Kimi Antonelli, has displayed on his way to a title he will almost surely secure this weekend at the Mexican Grand Prix.Antonelli was still a teenager for the first half of the year and it seemed fitting to describe him as such. His exuberant embrace of competing for Mercedesat the sharp end of F1in just his second season was that of any 19-year-old. Like discovering a life-changing new band or how much fun can be had with a cold beer, a wide grin was barely off his face.George Russell determined not to let disappointing F1 season define careerRead moreHe is 20 now, still but a stripling and on Sunday at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez if he finishes in ninth place or better he will be F1’s youngest world champion, and the first Italian to win the title since Alberto Ascari in 1953.Antonelli has confessed that as a four-year-old he did not recall when Sebastian Vettel became the previous youngest title winner in 2010. “I remember I was playing with Hot Wheels, but I don’t remember him clinching it,” he said.This weekend he will likely embrace an unforgettable moment. Antonelli has shone on track, at home with the complex requirements of the new energy-managed cars, extracting a pace and control such that even his more experienced Mercedes teammate George Russellhas been left flailingin his wake. To which traits he has allied a sharp and incisive driving style that has been extraordinary at times and a judgment that has belied his years.That he has done so with such alacrity, especially after a difficult rookie season last year, has surprised many. Not least those team principal Toto Wolff pointedly observed had been questioning whether Antonelli should even be in F1 after his debut season. Doubts now assuredly consigned to the dustbin of history, in the city where Leon Trotsky, who coined the phrase, was killed in 1940.It has been clear how much the Italian loves what he does and how that has informed his performances. At his shoulder through the trials of last season and the triumphs of this, has been Peter Bonnington. Bono, as he is known, was Lewis Hamilton’s engineer across the British driver’s six titles with Mercedes. He and Antonelli have established a close relationship, a friendship, with the Italian taking on board his colleague’s experience and cool head, often referencing him and the importance of their interaction.During Antonelli’s run of five successive victories in the opening period of the season, the last of them was astriking performance in Monaco. Taking an exceptional pole position to deny Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, who was in fearsome form on the streets of the principality, he then delivered a remarkable race win, including seeing off two restarts.View image in fullscreenKimi Antonelli is likely to be celebrating his historic title triumph this weekend in Mexico.Photograph: Robbie Hoad/Every Second Media/ShutterstockAfter this, Bono, who often has the avuncular air of an older brother with his young charge, gave an almost disarmingly straightforward explanation of what made his driver so quick.“As soon as he’s happy in the car: happy driver, fast lap time,” he said. The team have adopted an approach to allow Antonelli the opportunity to ensure he could drive in a way that allowed him to truly embrace being himself and in so doing, taking the pressure off.Bonningham described this as “giving him the freedom to do what he enjoys, giving him the freedom to enjoy driving the car, that’s a real big thing and not stressing too much. He’s just a joy to work with.”To trust the youngster’s instincts and talent, when the temptation to micromanage him must have been overwhelming, has worked brilliantly. Even as the opposition caught and at times surpassed Mercedes, Antonelli was able to deliver when a win was off the table. When it was, as at the last round in Austin, he stepped up to sweep it away with a nonchalance that typified why he is world champion elect.This makes the atmosphere in Mexico City all the more febrile in what is already one of the most vibrant venues on the calendar. Antonelli could barely have chosen a better location to enjoy the celebration of his childhood dream. The fans here embrace F1 with the same passion the Italian has for his trade.With the race coinciding with Mexico’s Day of the Dead, the city and the paddock are adorned with the bright orange Mexican marigolds, the“flor de muerto”. Skulls and skeletons, candles and colour are plentiful to welcome the return of the departed in a joyful, festival lending the weekend an already celebratory air.View image in fullscreenThe race coincides with Mexico’s Day of the Dead.Photograph: Marcel van Dorst/DeFodi Images/ShutterstockThe F1 faithful are also in good cheer in welcoming home hero Sergio Pérez back to the grid, with Cadillac and his image everywhere in Mexico City. On occasion he appears as a lifesize cardboard cut-out, rather incongruously in a line of fabulously-dressed skeletons. Yet fans will also doubtless revel in having this marvellous venue celebrate F1’s youngest champion in the heady atmosphere of the stadium section of Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez.Hamilton has experienced it twice, when he sealed the title here in 2017 and 2018, and the seven-time champion’s assessment of Antonelli’s season was as telling as that of his former race engineer.“You never know how anyone’s going to do under pressure until you see them,” he said. “I could assume that he was going to be fine with the weight you have on you. When you have to do all these appearances and all these things, pulled left, right and centre. But he’s taken it in his stride. He’s a relatively old soul in that young body.”Antonelli was withdrawn from his media duties on Thursday, with Mercedes saying he was unwell and needing to recover properly, but the Italian has stated he would like to finish the job in style and be able to relax for the remaining four races. There is no reason to believe he will suffer from any yips, certainly. He has demonstrated no such weakness thus far, even under the most intense pressure, with team principal Wolff sharing a further insight into why the 20-year-old stands ready to make history.“In Austin, he came to my office sat down on the sofa and said: ‘I’m going to enjoy this one. Isn’t it funny? I’m not thinking at all about the championship,’” Wolff recalled. “I said: ‘Stick to that attitude. You have the best job in the world. Don’t forget that.’ He has the right mindset.”The best job in the world and one he has, admirably, embraced with that irrepressible joy. The right mindset indeed. A deserved champion awaiting his coronation. On this form, not for the last time.In first practice in Mexico City, Ferrari once more opened strongly with Charles Leclerc topping the timesheets, six-tenths up on Antonelli in second, with the Italian apparently fully fit after Thursday’s illness. Many of the teams used the session to allow their rookie drivers to rack up track time with 10 taking part. The Danish driver Fredrik Vesti sat in for Russell and was in third, with Hamilton in fourth.In the afternoon session Hamilton lost vital running time when he retired with a loss of power after 30 minutes. His teammate Leclerc was once more quickest, one-tenth up on Lando Norris’s McLaren. Russell and Antonelli were in third and fourth and Red Bull’s Max Verstappen in fifth, three-tenths back, although the Dutchman was carrying some damage after a clash with Liam Lawson that will be investigated by the stewards.Explore more on these topicsFormula One 2026Kimi AntonelliMercedes GPFormula OneMotor sportfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: How can playing for Manchester City fit into Marc Guéhi’s moral universe? | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: Club’s predicament raises interesting questions about principles, both for individuals and the Premier League
Author: Barney Ronay
Headline: Club’s predicament raises interesting questions about principles, both for individuals and the Premier League
Content: Guéhi is playing for a club that has been convicted of cheating and lying. People are free to disagree with the rules. But if others are sticking to them, this amounts to deceit, stolen win bonuses, stolen glory. And the Bible is very clear on this.Illustration: Nathan Daniels/The GuardianView image in fullscreenGuéhi is playing for a club that has been convicted of cheating and lying. People are free to disagree with the rules. But if others are sticking to them, this amounts to deceit, stolen win bonuses, stolen glory. And the Bible is very clear on this.Illustration: Nathan Daniels/The GuardianManchester CityHow can playing for Manchester City fit into Marc Guéhi’s moral universe?Barney RonayClub’s predicament raises interesting questions about principles, both for individuals and the Premier LeagueFri 30 Oct 2026 16.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 30 Oct 2026 18.59 EDTShareI felt unbelievably ponderous. My head was made of Aztec stone. I realised I didn’t want to be with all these people. Somebody came at me, a huge individual in silver and blue. I fell at his feet and grabbed one shoe. I started untying the lace. He kicked away from me. I got up and walked off. I was exceedingly hungry.Not my words. Also not the words of theManchester Citycentre-back Marc Guéhi, despite what you were thinking there. This is instead a condensed quote from the mind of Gary Harkness, existentially curious college running-back and the narrator of Don DeLillo’s great American football novel End Zone.This passage describes a moment where Gary plays a game having been urged by his friends to smoke pot beforehand to discover whether it improves his understanding of time and space, or just makes him want to lie down and untie someone’s laces. It marks a turning point for Gary. To this point football has been a comforting world. He sees clarity in its militaristic rituals, finds in sport “the illusion that order is possible”, hears hidden truths in the coaches’ shouted instructions. Button up. Get fetal. Get fetal. Get fetal. Run with reckless abandon.Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekendRead moreNow the illusion has collapsed. Gary walks off the football field and begins instead to fixate on cold war fears and nuclear apocalypse. Death and political power have entered the chat.Now, I’m not saying Marc Guéhi is Gary Harkness. You might be saying that. That’s your choice. But Guéhi has seemed a bit distracted in the last few weeks. Oddly for an agile and technically sound centre-back, he has seemed brittle and absent, vulnerable to being pressed.There have been a couple of things said about City’s players in this regard. The first is that their minds might not be wholly on the game, that in the middle of a game against Croatia, for example, concerned only with manoeuvring through tiny pockets of space, Nico O’Reilly is also thinking: “Hmm, but how is it possible even by omission to honestly contravene rules E.3 and E.4 which state clearly that …oh. Wait, no. Oh dear.”Football doesn’t work like this. The physical game is a place of total focus. But still, nothing is watertight. And this speaks to the second thing people have said, repeated like an absolute truth, that the players are entirely separate from all this. They cannot be questioned here, or indeed expected to ask questions of their own. The players are simply avatars, employees, free from any kind of agency. Players don’t have access to Google. They cannot make moral judgments. And yes, this may not be true of any other human in any other field. It may be the case that elite footballers are in fact unusually empowered, free to do whatever they want. But the consensus is clear. It is not a footballer’s business to have opinions on their employers, or what happens out of their line of vision.This does help to avoid some tricky conundrums. Guéhi, for example, is a man of absolute public principle. Fair enough. I respect his willingness to resist popular pressure and personalise his support for the rainbow armband by writing things about Jesus on top of it. This is living your values. It’s free speech, figuring out your own moral universe. Doing so by following the absolute tenets of his religion. Go for it.At the same time, Guéhi is playing for a club that has been convicted of cheating and lying. People are free to disagree with the rules. But if others are sticking to them, this amounts to deceit, stolen win bonuses, stolen glory. And the Bible is very clear on this. Thessalonians 4:6: “No one should transgress and defraud his brother.” Proverbs 20:17: “Bread gained by deceit is sweet to a man, but afterward his mouth will be full of gravel.” Now, I don’t believe these words to be divinely ordained. They’re great words. Totally dig the vibe. But Guéhi does believe these things to be an absolute instruction. How does this fit together in his head? How does that gravel (pending appeal) taste right now?View image in fullscreenThe physical game is a place of total focus. But still, nothing is watertight.Photograph: Matt West/ShutterstockAgain, fine if you can square it. It’s a personal journey. Park the apparent moral dilemma. See if your legal team can come up with a better final outcome. But things have changed in one significant way since the verdict dropped, an element that is now unchallenged, and which has been largely unremarked in the middle of the chaos. Understandably so. This stuff is gruelling. Everyone just wants to watch some football in the brief lull between legal rage events. But there are two points worth making in the interim. The second of which is an admission that affects many other things.The first issue is: do you actually understand the basis of the Manchester City appeal? That evidence has seemingly been leaked. The irrefutable body of evidence, Body Of Evidence 2, the long-awaited tribunal-based Madonna erotic thriller vehicle, contains a vital detail: the additional money in City’s coffers, almost a billion, did not come from the owners, the Abu Dhabi United Group, which is owned, like City, by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan. This would be against the rules. It came instead from the Abu Dhabi government, which is essentially the Abu Dhabi royal family, of which Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan is a member; as he is also, wearing a different hat, of the Abu Dhabi government.And maybe this means it’s fine. It seems the government often tops up the sponsor companies like a benevolent uncle. In the period the charges relate to there was no need for sponsor deals to be of market value, as there is now. So if we accept all this, if we can establish a binding principle of wearing different hats in different rooms, this may be a way out. Maybe.This is a familiar concept in the high court, in an age of shell companies and tricky fiscal flows. Mega-million cases hang on whether ownership really is separate, or whether this is, to echo a phrase, a sham process. The person on the Clapham omnibus might not buy any of this. Do these really seem like separate entities? Or a bit like adopting a French accent when the bailiffs ring up and maintaining that, no, Monsieur Ronay is not here, and he definitely doesn’t run this dry cleaners. That, instead, is me.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIf you make the case you win the case. This is all in the end about the application of rules, and that is a good thing. But the key point here is the secondary issue derived from this. City’s leaked defence, in making their case, is also saying, without pretence or mucking about, that the club is indeed funded by the Abu Dhabi government. This is something City’s fans have at times weirdly denied. But we have it in plain sight now, not just admitted but insisted on. The ultimate source of the dizzying success of the club that has defined a Premier League era is the government. Guéhi is, in effect, an Abu Dhabi civil servant. Perhaps the United Arab Emirates national team should have six stars on their jersey, one for each Premier League won. But there is no way of covering your ears now. City actively want us to accept this.What are the consequences of this new fact? It comes with two urgent questions. The first is the moral one. Back again to Guéhi as the best example. This is what he is promoting here. And Guéhi is a man entirely guided by the principles of his faith. A private matter perhaps, except that it’s not, because Guéhi’s church explicitly orders its members to go out and proselytise. Guéhi is a member of Ballers in God, which actively tries to awaken Christian faith in the dressing room. He plays with Christian messages on his matchday kit intended to make you, the reader, think yes, maybe I too should follow this evangelical church.Manchester City guilty over Premier League charges after £900m of ‘sham’ contractsRead moreAnd here is the key thing. This is a criminal offence in Abu Dhabi. Under UAE penal code, giving out Christian leaflets will get you arrested. A Christian pastor in the UAE was sentenced to a year in prison for giving a Muslim a Bible. Some Americans were deported for giving out Christian literature in the Dubai shopping district. Spreading the gospel, which Guéhi is morally bound to do, is illegal in the place that pays his direct employers.Are players just avatars, empty shells? How much do you really believe in this? These are, more than ever, very interesting questions. And they don’t just apply to issues of personal principle.The regulator now has this information, too. Abu Dhabi funded the purchase of Nolito. Abu Dhabi dictated the flow of English football finance. The same pocket that paid for this is also funding at arm’s length the civil war in Sudan, the hospital massacres, the piles of bodies so high they can be seen from satellite imaging. Abu Dhabi, which criminalises homosexuality, which crushes dissent, is openly identifying itself as the mega-funder of a Premier League club. Is this a fit and proper influence?There are very obvious reasons why this is not desirable. Governments spy and wage war and break rules. They have a sacred trust to promote their own interests by any means necessary. It is hard to see how this kind of owner fits the regulatory framework. Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund had to twirl through semantic hoops when buying Newcastle to establish it was an entity at one remove from a government, as opposed to a government entity. In making the opposite case for their funding City have not only exposed their own live-your-values central defender, they have put themselves in a place where, even if you win on one front, you’ve started to look like a very strange presence.This deserves to be unravelled in all its wider implications. It may be the biggest issue here, whatever the final verdict. How can this be the right thing? How can City’s fans look their own autocratic government-funded club in the eye? The quiet thing has been said out loud. And its implications are bigger than the game, bigger than legal opinion. Enough, perhaps to make you question the existential point of this thing, where the best course of action really might be to walk off and look for the nearest cheeseburger.Explore more on these topicsManchester CitycommentShareReuse this content

title: Packers’ Josh Jacobs says hands-behind-back TD celebration was not mocking recent arrest | NFL | The Guardian
description: The Green Bay running back said he was referencing a song called Break Every Chain when celebrating a touchdown by putting his hands behind his back
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The Green Bay running back said he was referencing a song called Break Every Chain when celebrating a touchdown by putting his hands behind his back
Content: Josh Jacobs celebrated a touchdown in Thursday night’s Packers game by putting his hands behind his back.Photograph: Stacy Revere/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenJosh Jacobs celebrated a touchdown in Thursday night’s Packers game by putting his hands behind his back.Photograph: Stacy Revere/Getty ImagesNFLPackers’ Josh Jacobs says hands-behind-back TD celebration was not mocking recent arrestGreen Bay RB claims gesture was an ode to gospel songJacobs pleaded no contest to battery charges last monthAssociated PressFri 30 Oct 2026 08.22 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGreen Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs says he was paying homage to a gospel song rather than making light of his recent arrest when he briefly had his hands behind his back while celebrating a touchdown Thursday night.This was Jacobs’s second game of the season after coming off the commissioner’s exempt list. He was placed on that list afterchargeswere filed against him in August stemming from a May altercation with his then-girlfriend during which she said he threw her to the ground.Jacobs pleaded no contest last month to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property.Packers beat Panthers as Green Bay’s Christian Watson returns after mid-game hospital visitRead moreJacobs had just scored on a one-yard run in the second quarter of the Packers’27-19victory over the Carolina Panthers when he put his hands behind his back for a moment while accepting congratulations from teammates. The video garnered attention on social media as some who watched on television believed Jacobs was simulating getting handcuffed.Jacobs said he instead was modeling his celebration after a gospel song called Break Every Chain.“The guys did it with me,” Jacobs said. “I didn’t think it was going to be a thing that can be perceived a certain type of way. But it’s 2026, and it is what it is.”Jacobs said he had spoken with teammate Savion Williams and other receivers before making his season debut, and they came up with the idea that he would do a celebration thanking God after his first touchdown of the season. That celebration happened Sunday, as he went to his knees and raised his arms aloft after scoring in a 20-17 loss at Detroit.They also had planned this Break Every Chain celebration after his second touchdown of the season. When Jacobs was asked about putting his hands behind his back as part of the celebration, he noted that the telecast only showed a brief portion of what he did.“It was more to it than that,” Jacobs said. “They stopped showing the celebration after that. Like I said, it is what it is.”Jacobs hadn’t been able to play or practice while he was on the commissioner’s exempt list. He was removed from that list last week, enabling him to play again even though the NFL’s investigation of him remains ongoing.Explore more on these topicsNFLUS sportsGreen Bay PackersnewsShareReuse this content

title: Carrick tells players ‘hard truth’ in attempt to turn Manchester United’s season around | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: The head coach, who said the players were ‘hurting’ after eight games without a win, reflected on ‘not always rosy and nice conversations’
Author: Will Unwin
Headline: The head coach, who said the players were ‘hurting’ after eight games without a win, reflected on ‘not always rosy and nice conversations’
Content: Michael Carrick is under intense pressure after defeats by Atlético Madrid, Como and Bournemouth in October.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAView image in fullscreenMichael Carrick is under intense pressure after defeats by Atlético Madrid, Como and Bournemouth in October.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAManchester UnitedCarrick tells players ‘hard truth’ in attempt to turn Manchester United’s season aroundHead coach reflects on ‘not always rosy’ conversationsPlayers ‘hurting’ after eight games without a winWill UnwinFri 30 Oct 2026 18.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMichael Carrick said he has had difficult conversations with theManchester Unitedhierarchy and his players during their turbulent start to the season.United have not won in their past eight games and start the weekend in 16th place of 20 in the league, one point above the relegation zone.The academy system needs a refresh but now is the time for Carrick to trust in youthRead moreCarrick’s position was under threat after losing last Sunday to Bournemouthbut he has held on to his jobfor the time being and been given the chance to turn things around, starting at Chelsea on Saturday.The head coach suggested he had spoken with the club’s director of football, Jason Wilcox, and the chief executive, Omar Berrada, this week.“It’s pretty clear, it’s not always rosy and nice conversations between anyone, whether that’s between me and the players, whether that’s between me, Jason, Omar or the owners,” Carrick said. “It’s the truth, it’s the hard truth at times and it’s what we need to move forward. Whatever we need to move forward, we will do.”The supporters cheered Carrick off after he did a lap of the pitch in the aftermath ofSunday’s 3-0 defeat, but once he entered the tunnel they booed the players after a poor performance and perceived lack of effort. Carrick said the players are “hurting” but are “hungry” to turn things around.“I’ll be totally honest, it was mixed feelings for me,” Carrick said. “To have the appreciation from the supporters and that connection and that respect is something I feel strongly about.“It wasn’t a nice situation but to feel that was important, of course, but it didn’t make me feel better in the fact that I’m with the players 100% and we’re all in it together. I’ve told the players that, I’m happy to say that.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“I didn’t feel comfortable being in any way, shape or form, a separation from that. That’s my group, my players and this is my football club so we have to all be in it together, and that’s the supporters included. As hard as it is at the moment, I totally get that, I get their feelings, but when we get through this then we’ll be a lot stronger as a whole.”Gary Neville questioned some of the players’ professionalism on his podcast this week. “I’ve got no time for them,” Neville said. “There’s a few of them that don’t go to bed at the right time. Don’t eat the right things.” Carrick laughed off the allegations with the remark: “Gaz says a lot of things.”Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedMichael CarricknewsShareReuse this content

title: Suspicious bets returning £149,000 for predicting Ballon d’Or under investigation | Ballon d'Or | The Guardian
description: A series of suspicious bets that correctly predicted the exact top-five finishing order of this year’s Ballon d’Or and generated almost $200,000 is being investigated
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: A series of suspicious bets that correctly predicted the exact top-five finishing order of this year’s Ballon d’Or and generated almost $200,000 is being investigated
Content: Harry Kane was crowned the winner at this year’s Ballon d’Or.Photograph: S Stingl/FC Bayern/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenHarry Kane was crowned the winner at this year’s Ballon d’Or.Photograph: S Stingl/FC Bayern/Getty ImagesBallon d'OrSuspicious bets returning £149,000 for predicting Ballon d’Or under investigationBets predicted exact top-five men’s finishing orderOrganiser France Football has contacted policeEd AaronsandRomain MolinaFri 30 Oct 2026 17.12 EDTLast modified on Fri 30 Oct 2026 17.55 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA series of suspicious bets that correctly predicted the exact top-five finishing order ofthis year’s Ballon d’Orand generated almost $200,000 (£149,000) in winnings is being investigated by the event’s organisers, France Football, who have also contacted the police.It has been alleged that 12 Polymarket accounts – an American cryptocurrency-based prediction market – placed the bets, with more than $264,000 wagered on the outcome before Monday’s ceremony. Their extraordinary accuracy has raised serious questions about a potential leak of confidential results before football’s most prestigious individual award.Harry Kane was crowned the winnerat the ceremony at the London Palladium, finishing ahead of Kylian Mbappé, Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Lionel Messi. Remarkably, this was the exact order predicted by the group of accounts identified in French media outletUpside’s investigation.According to Raphaël Pautard, the co-founder of Upside, his team identified 12 Polymarket accounts created between 1 October and 20 October. The accounts displayed strikingly similar patterns of activity, leading investigators to suspect they could be connected to the same individual or group. Seven of the 12 accounts had not participated in any other betting markets, while six placed their first bets 15 minutes after being created.Pautard revealed that his team managed to trace one transaction back to a French platform. After sharing the relevant blockchain transactions and wallet addresses with the company’s team, the platform reportedly confirmed it had identified the individual behind one of the accounts involved in funding the suspicious bets. The identity of that individual has not been publicly disclosed, but the development could prove significant in establishing connections between the accounts and tracing the money behind the wagers.Quick GuideHow do I sign up for sport breaking news alerts?ShowIn the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from theiOS App Storeon iPhone or theGoogle Play storeon Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Upside passed its findings to France Football, which Groupe Amaury owns and which has organised the awards since 1956. It is understood to have received confirmation on Friday afternoon that an investigation has been opened, with the French police also to be informed. France Football has been contacted for comment.Rather than spreading their money across different outcomes, the accounts concentrated their wagers on a specific scenario: Kane winning, followed by Mbappé in second, Yamal in third, Rodri in fourth and Messi in fifth. Every position subsequently matched the official results, generating nearly $200,000 in profits.According to the investigation by Upside, one account purchased a contract predicting Kane would win at 37 cents before selling it when the price reached 67 cents. The funds were subsequently redirected towards bets on specific finishing positions, including Yamal finishing third. This sequence of transactions has attracted attention because it suggests the account holder adjusted their strategy as the relevant markets developed.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBefore the ceremony, France Football had indicated that only a handful of people knew the winner in advance. The possibility that confidential information could have reached betting accounts before the official announcement is therefore a serious concern, particularly given the precision of the predictions and the amount of money involved. “How do we keep the winner’s identity hidden? I think a well-kept secret is one that is shared with as few people as possible,” said the former France Football editor Pascal Ferré last week.Explore more on these topicsBallon d'OrnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘It’s just USA, blah, blah, blah’: Rising rugby star Bella Vogel out to catch wounded England napping | USA women's rugby union team | The Guardian
description: The Pennsylvania center found rugby early and is nominated for World Rugby Breakthrough Player of the Year. In New Jersey, the Red Roses will present her stiffest Test yet
Author: Martin Pengelly
Headline: The Pennsylvania center found rugby early and is nominated for World Rugby Breakthrough Player of the Year. In New Jersey, the Red Roses will present her stiffest Test yet
Content: Bella Vogel in action against New Zealand.Photograph: Travis Prior/Travis Prior/USA RugbyView image in fullscreenBella Vogel in action against New Zealand.Photograph: Travis Prior/Travis Prior/USA RugbyUSA women's rugby union team‘It’s just USA, blah, blah, blah’: Rising rugby star Bella Vogel out to catch wounded England nappingThe Pennsylvania center found rugby early and is nominated for World Rugby Breakthrough Player of the Year. In New Jersey, the Red Roses will present her stiffest Test yetMartin PengellyFri 30 Oct 2026 05.00 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGoing into their WXV Global Series game against England’s world champion Red Roses in Harrison, New Jersey, on Friday, the US Eagles women have five successive wins and a squad mixing great experience with great youth. Among potentially great younger players is the first American ever nominated for a major World Rugby award.“I keep getting told like, ‘Oh, don’t let your head get too big,’” laughed Bella Vogel, the 19-year-old center or fly-half from Washington Boro, Pennsylvania,nominatedfor Women’s 15s Breakthrough Player of the Year. Still a student atLife University in Marietta, Georgia, she has had an extraordinary season.“Honestly, like in my head, yes, I [was nominated] but I could not have done it without the team,” Vogel said, previewing the England game alongside the Eagles coach, Jack Hanratty. “They make me look good. My job is to make other people look good, but I just give the ball to Freda, and she runs through 10 people.”Freda Tafuna, the US No 8, is only 23. Out of Lindenwood University in St Charles, Missouri, she won theMA Sorensen Awardfor college player of the year twice before taking part in the World Cup in England last year. She shone there, scoring two tries against Australia andfour against Samoa. Last Saturday in Nashville, Tennessee, Tafuna scored three ina 54-24 winover Italy.That lifted the US one place to sixth in theworld rankings. England are first. The last time the teams met, in the World Cup opener in front of 43,000,England won 69-7. But the women’s game is shifting a little. At the top, the Red Roses’ 41-game, four-year unbeaten streak ended this month withtwo defeats by Canada. The Eagles contest supremacy in an improving middle tier, having beaten Ireland and Australia this year.Asked what England might now know about his team, Hanratty said: “They know the No 8. Freda has been incredible with the carry meters. I would say they know more of our names … We have had good entries into the 22. So how do we get in there? We’ve had great try rates. How are we scoring? I’d say all of this information will be done and they’ll be looking at our defense and trying to test us in new ways. They’ve got multiple kickers on the field. They’ve got lots of speed on the field. So they’ll be challenging us in a way that other teams maybe haven’t or look to exploit some of the weaknesses that we don’t even know we have yet, and that’s the great test for Friday. What do we think they’re going to do, and how do we stop it? And that’s what’s exciting for me and for the players.”Vogel, Tafuna and other young Eagles show signs of taking such tests in their stride. The key point is that many found the game much younger than has been usual in the US, where most discover rugby at college, as the story of Hall of Fame flankerPhaidra Knightshows well. Homeschooled in rural Pennsylvania, working the family farm, a devout Christian, Vogelstartedplaying rugby at 10. Playing forKnightmare Rugby, a club in Lancaster, PA, she regularly facedDoylestownand their own talented back,Nina Mason. Both ended up at Life, an elite program under highly regarded coachRyszard Chadwick. Mason is now the Eagles fly-half with Vogel at 12.The emergence of such young talent is key to the Eagles’ improvement now and will be in future. By kick-off at the 2033 Women’s World Cup, in the US, Mason and Vogel will be 26, in their athletic prime.Hanratty is giving them every chance to learn. In April, in Sacramento, California, Vogel started on debut against the mighty Black Ferns of New Zealand. A48-15 defeatwas full of lessons and Vogel stayed in the team, working with Mason to launch back play – Vogel’s slashing break for one ofcaptain Georgie Perris-Redding’sthree tries in game one against Italy,won 36-27, stood out – or marshal forward raids around the ruck by Tafuna and her smash-happy pals. Vogel does the goal-kicking, with impressive success.Vogel has alsofacedAustralia, Canada, South Africa, Ireland and Wales. She’s unlikely to be fazed on Friday night but this is still England, wounded by two defeats.“I definitely think that England’s gonna be a tough game, and I think that all their fans are gonna be like, ‘Oh, it’s just USA, blah blah blah,’” Vogel said, perhaps still sensing a chance to sneak under the Red Roses’ radar. “I remember there was a post, and it was like, ’Canada, England, and USA are the only teams that haven’t, like. lost a game’ [in WXV]. And people in the comments were like, ‘Oh, why would you compare England to USA?’ I think this is our chance to show them that we are comparable, and that we are just as good as any top-three team.”To Hanratty, the WXV Global Series “has been a huge success,” producing competitive matches at a greater rate, England and Canada producing a classic three-Test series won by the Canadians with two home wins after a draw in England, the Eagles fighting out a1-1 draw in South Africathen taking tough wins in Ireland and Wales, and the 2-0 home win over Italy.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe BreakdownThe latest rugby union news and analysis, plus all the week's action reviewedEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“England are a brilliant rugby team,” Hanratty said. “They won 40 games on the trot. Theywon a Rugby World Cupwhile doing it, and at times they were untested in certain areas. We’ve been able to grind out wins against teams that have beaten us quite comfortably over the last number of years, and the bookies would say would have again, and we’ve had some really great moments.”Expecting England to make every bit of use of an extra day of recovery, Hanratty expected a fierce blast from a team out to “not only show the world that they’re still number one, and to do that would be not only winning the game but showing dominance in everything.“Our job this week is to challenge them. We want to see what aspects of the game have we grown in, that we can challenge the world’s best. That’s our job. I think we’ve got a bit of an opportunity for a free hit, but I love the fact that we’re coming into it with momentum. It’s at the end of an eight-week tour, and it’s amazing that our meetings are still energetic, our training sessions are still actually of quality.” He also welcomed “the fact that we get to play at home against the world champions to end Bella’s first year, to end my own first year, and to end this squad’s first year of what hopefully would be an incredible World Cup cycle.”USA v England and USA men v Australia XV will be broadcast in the USon Paramount Plusand in the UK on theEngland Rugby YouTube channelandBBC iPlayer.Martin Pengelly writes about rugby in the US on Substack, atThe National Maul.Explore more on these topicsUSA women's rugby union teamRugby unionWomen's rugby unionfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Aston Villa to take legal action against Jamie Carragher for ‘unacceptable insults’ | Aston Villa | The Guardian
description: Aston Villa have announced plans to take legal action against Jamie Carragher following his “unacceptable insults” about the club and its supporters
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Aston Villa have announced plans to take legal action against Jamie Carragher following his “unacceptable insults” about the club and its supporters
Content: Jamie Carragher upset Aston Villa with comments he made on the Stick to Football podcast.Photograph: Mike Egerton/PAView image in fullscreenJamie Carragher upset Aston Villa with comments he made on the Stick to Football podcast.Photograph: Mike Egerton/PAAston VillaAston Villa to take legal action against Jamie Carragher for ‘unacceptable insults’Villa chair announces plan on social mediaCarragher said club will ‘never be Man United’Press AssociationFri 30 Oct 2026 19.55 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAston Villa have announced plans to take legal action againstJamie Carragherfollowing his “unacceptable insults” about the club and its supporters.Carragher told Villa fans to “shut the fuck up” after facing criticism for suggesting Unai Emery should consider taking the Manchester United job. Villa responded on Friday evening with a statement on X signed by their chair, Nassef Sawiris.“Aston Villa will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher for his unacceptable insults about the club and its fans,” the statement said. “Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football. Nassef Sawiris, chairman.”Former Liverpool defender Carragher made his remarks on the Stick to Football podcast while discussing the prospect of Emery replacing Michael Carrick at Old Trafford. The 48-year-old Sky Sports pundit argued there was a hierarchy in football, saying “Aston Villa will never be Man United”.“I’m not trying to annoy Villa fans but there is a chain in football, whether you like it or not,” said Carragher. “So Real Madrid will take Man United’s best player, they’ll take [Cristiano] Ronaldo. There’s very few above United, the same with Liverpool.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“But there will be teams below Aston Villa and they [Villa] will take their manager or they will take their players, so shut the fuck up Villa fans. Aston Villa will never be Man United.”Explore more on these topicsAston VillaJamie CarraghernewsShareReuse this content

title: Xabi Alonso rules out January loan move for Chelsea winger Estêvão Willian | Chelsea | The Guardian
description: The Chelsea manager said of a potential move for Estêvão after only two starts in 11 games: ‘No discussions about that … Everyone has to be ready’
Author: Jacob Steinberg
Headline: The Chelsea manager said of a potential move for Estêvão after only two starts in 11 games: ‘No discussions about that … Everyone has to be ready’
Content: Estêvão Willian was an unused substitute against Liverpool in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday.Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenEstêvão Willian was an unused substitute against Liverpool in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday.Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/ReutersChelseaXabi Alonso rules out January loan move for Chelsea winger Estêvão Willian‘No discussions about that … Everyone has to be ready’Brazilian has started only twice in 11 games this seasonJacob SteinbergFri 30 Oct 2026 18.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleXabi Alonso has ruled out a January move for Estêvão Willian but has said the Chelsea youngster must adapt to his style of play before earning a regular spot in the team.The debate around Estêvão’s role gathered momentum this week, with the noise growing after the 19-year-old watched as an unused substitute asAlonso’s side lost to Liverpoolon penalties in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday. The Brazilian became an instant hit with Chelsea fans after joining from Palmeiras last year and there are fears that the winger could look to leave after starting twice in 11 games in all competitions this season.Estêvão ready to rival Lamine Yamal in battle of the teenage prodigiesRead moreYet while Estêvão is having a tougher time during his second year in English football, Alonso insisted that the Brazil international is part of his plans and will not be loaned out to get more games in January.“No discussions about that,” Alonso said. “It’s no secret that all players want to be on the pitch. When any of them haven’t had enough minutes because of my decision, I have to take the responsibility for that. But everyone has to be ready because in any game they could be important. Este, his training and his attitude has been good.”There was a lot of hype around Estêvão after his £51.4m move. He impressed last season, particularly when he scored a brilliantsolo goal against Barcelona, only for a hamstring injury to dash his hopes of going to the World Cup.The teenager has struggled since returning from injury. Estêvão has played a total of 47 minutes in the Premier League this season. He earned an international recall from Carlo Ancelotti on Thursday but is yet to convince Alonso, who explained the process for Estêvão from a tactical perspective beforeChelseahost Manchester United on Saturday.“Well [it is] in the adaptation to the competition, the process to learn things with the ball, against the ball, how to be more competitive,” Alonso said. “That’s for all the players who have made that big step to the Premier League. I am part of the process to help him. For sure I understand the moment, I understand his feeling. It’s still early days.”Alonso did not use all of his substitutions against Liverpool. He suggested physicality was a reason for Estêvão’s omission after the game. On Friday, Alonso said that improving without the ball is not the only issue.“It’s one thing,” he said. “With the ball is very important as well. That’s sometimes when to take the right decision, what to do in the next situation. It’s to keep the ball, it’s to find the right pass. And, as well, against the ball you need to be competitive. That’s in football and in the Premier League mandatory now.“The demand of the Premier League is higher than other leagues because of the tempo. To be there as a teenager is not easy. That’s why to go through this filter is not for everyone. It takes time. Even then there will be mistakes. Mistakes are part of the learning process.”Alonso has often used a 3-4-2-1 system, with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers playing as No 10s. He considered whether Estêvão would be suited to a role in the middle.“Depending on the game, the context, he could play more in this pocket position as a No 10,” he said. “But where he has played more in the Premier League has been as a winger. In one-on-one situations he has good moments.”Chelsea have selection issues in defence before facing United. Jorrel Hato has a back problem and Maxence Lacroix is out until after the international break after sustaining a hamstring injury against Liverpool.Explore more on these topicsChelseaXabi AlonsonewsShareReuse this content

title: Grealish could have been Everton’s poster boy of a new era. Now his career is in limbo | Everton | The Guardian
description: After being dropped for ‘a breach of club discipline’, the winger must face the same questions about respect and self-awareness
Author: Will Unwin
Headline: After being dropped for ‘a breach of club discipline’, the winger must face the same questions about respect and self-awareness
Content: Jack Grealish’s contract at Manchester City ends this summer, so there is incentive to show he is capable of shining in the Premier League.Photograph: Molly Darlington/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenJack Grealish’s contract at Manchester City ends this summer, so there is incentive to show he is capable of shining in the Premier League.Photograph: Molly Darlington/Getty ImagesEvertonGrealish could have been Everton’s poster boy of a new era. Now his career is in limboAfter being dropped for ‘a breach of club discipline’, the winger must face the same questions about respect and self-awarenessWill UnwinFri 30 Oct 2026 12.50 EDTLast modified on Fri 30 Oct 2026 14.10 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFor the biggest game in Manchester City’s history, Jack Grealish was given a starting berth while Phil Foden, Julián Alvarez and Riyad Mahrez were on the bench. Grealish played the full 90 minutes of theChampions League triumph against Interbecause Pep Guardiola had the greatest faith in the attacking midfielder, but three years on he is at risk of being yesterday’s man.That trust dwindled, not helped by injuries, and Grealish made only 17 Premier League starts over the next two seasons under Guardiola. City wanted him to leave in the summer of 2025, and Everton provided the solution, taking him on loan and borrowing him again for this season. Six Everton appearances into this campaign he was left out of the squad for Thursday’sCarabao Cup win against Newcastleafter missing training on Monday. Everton went public with the fact that there had been “a breach of club discipline”.Everton drop Jack Grealish from Carabao Cup tie over ‘breach of club discipline’Read moreGrealish is 31 and has 39 England caps. He is supposed to be a senior player but his career has involved far too many indiscretions. Breaking lockdown rules, a driving ban and more than once becoming a viral sensation for being pictured inebriated out and about have painted an unwanted picture. Learning from mistakes is part of life but Grealish’s indiscipline is apparently not dwindling with age. Guardiola warned him over his behaviour, dropping him in 2021 for a match against Newcastle after he and Foden arrived for training worse for wear.Grealish is aware of his flaws, which is a starting point, but dealing with them is a separate matter. “People go: ‘He likes to go out, he likes to party,’ and I do,” Grealish told Sky Sports last year. “I want to be able to live my life and enjoy myself but obviously there’s a time and a place to do that. Sometimes, I’ll be honest with you, I probably haven’t picked the right times.”Initially atEvertonit seemed Grealish could be the poster boy of a new era. There were winners against Crystal Palace and Bournemouth by early December of last year and he had accumulated six assists in 20 Premier League appearances before his season was ended in mid-January by a foot injury. Grealish had been inconsistent, though. He has not played more than 28 league games in a season since 2019-20 at Aston Villa, which should concern him.There were reservations at Everton about taking Grealish back this summer but Iliman Ndiaye’s sale to City made it a pragmatic move to fill the void. Grealish had carried out pre-season under Enzo Maresca, who gave him chances in the Community Shield and on the opening day against Bournemouth. The Italian had time for him but the unlikely redemption arc at City was soon quashed. Maresca showed affection for Grealish on Friday, saying: “I still think that he’s a good boy, big heart.”View image in fullscreenDavid Moyes was terse on the subject of Jack Grealish and seems unlikely to recommend keeping him beyond the length of his current loan.Photograph: Tony McArdle/Everton FC/Getty ImagesAt his best, Grealish is a wonderful player, a carefree spirit when dribbling with his socks around his ankles. In full flow, he gets fans up off their seats, makes and takes goalscoring chances and forces opponents to foul him, but those moments have been fleeting for far too long. The next seven months are crucial to Grealish’s career; he is at an age where he could play at the top for years but his status is declining rapidly. He is a £100m City signing and treble winner but those are past glories. Grealish needs to prove he has the respect for himself and for Everton to want more.Grealish’s contract at City concludes at the end of the season, so there is plenty of incentive for him to show he is capable of shining in the Premier League and inspiring Everton to the cup win they crave. Instead, his career is in limbo. David Moyes was terse on the subject of Grealish on Thursday and seems unlikely to recommend keeping him beyond his loan. The Everton manager is working with a very small squad, so losing a senior player for avoidable reasons will surely frustrate and irritate him.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIn an industry where the public is kept at arm’s length, Grealish is very approachable, happy to sign autographs for longer than his peers, eager to do the charity elements that come with playing for major clubs and known for his personal touch when others are businesslike. When entering and leaving Hill Dickinson Stadium, Grealish is mobbed, such is his popularity. He embraces it, posing for selfies with anyone who demands one, channelling a lot of positive energy into others, but he needs to find the self-awareness to do the same for himself.“With me, I’m a big confidence player – I want to feel loved,” Grealish once said. He will not be feeling that from Moyes any time soon without radical change.Explore more on these topicsEvertonfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Putellas provides mindset change as London City bid to upstage champions | Women's Super League | The Guardian
description: Ballon d’Or winner’s move to WSL has transformed the Lionesses on and off the pitch with belief soaring ahead of Manchester City clash
Author: Tom Garry
Headline: Ballon d’Or winner’s move to WSL has transformed the Lionesses on and off the pitch with belief soaring ahead of Manchester City clash
Content: London City Lionesses will go head-to-head with Manchester City in a eagerly anticipated showdown this weekend.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianView image in fullscreenLondon City Lionesses will go head-to-head with Manchester City in a eagerly anticipated showdown this weekend.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianWomen's Super LeaguePutellas provides mindset change as London City bid to upstage championsBallon d’Or winner’s move to WSL has transformed the Lionesses on and off the pitch with belief soaring ahead of Manchester City clashTom GarryFri 30 Oct 2026 12.16 EDTLast modified on Fri 30 Oct 2026 13.42 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAs Martin Semmens, the London City Lionesses chief executive, sits down is his office he looks like the cat that got the cream. He says he has just learned that the club’s Instagram page has generated 34m hits since Alexia Putellaswon the Ballon d’Oron Monday evening, and it is only Thursday afternoon. On Sunday, two clubs with seven of the top 30 players in the Ballon d’Or rankings will go head-to-head when Manchester City visit Hayes Lane, Bromley. It is, Semmens, says, “awesome for the WSL”.From the outside, it can feel slightly surreal. The independent women’s club, owned by the businesswoman Michele Kang, are third in the top flight, two‑and‑a‑half years after finishing eighth in tier two, and Semmens believessigning the world’s best playerhas helped change the mindset of everyone at the club.Fifa to miss equal Women’s World Cup prize money ambition set by InfantinoRead more“Her impact on our commercial business is extraordinary,” he says. “From a leadership point of view, she allows us to start thinking about really winning. The environment today feels like it can beat Man City on Sunday and that’s a lot down to her.”He acknowledges that Putellas, a World Cup winner with Spain and four-time European champion with Barcelona, and her brand – she has more Instagram followers (3.7m) than a men’s club the size of Porto, for example – were pivotal in helping the club secure what they claim is the largest front-of-shirt sponsorship deal in the women’s game, with Nike. The club say it is worth more than the new NWSL franchise Atlanta’s sponsorship of $4m (£3m) a year.“It’s insanely big,” Semmens says. “Our view on how to run this business, rightly or wrongly, was to invest first, invest in the everything to make it awesome, and then the commercial deal will be big. The other way, of: ‘Let’s sit back, let’s grow a fanbase, let’s wait for the money to come’ – we don’t have the patience for that. Michele’s vision was: ‘I’m going to invest now to prove that we can bring these deals in.’ That deal allows us to kick forward, it allows us to keep investing in players and infrastructure, because without it, we’re just burning Michele’s money, which is not the plan.”Even with Kang’s money, signing a player who had been loyal to Barcelona for 14 years was never going to be straightforward. Semmens, the former Southampton chief executive, says: “The conversation went: ‘Wait until I’ve finished winning a Champions League with Barcelona and then we’ll have a conversation,’ which we loved and we respected, but we always had a feeling she would come.View image in fullscreenAlexia Putellas has provided a huge commercial lift to the club.Photograph: Alex Ferrelly/Sports Press Photo/Shutterstock“I think she had bought into four or five significant things. One, that we are independent, we’re a women’s-first environment. [Two] there’s a lot of power in coming to London, as a city. The WSL is important – people see WSL as the growth brand. And, after that, Michele had an unbelievably massive impact [on Putellas’s decision]. Alexia said to me: ‘Well, she said she was going to do all this stuff and she’s done it. So I want to be part of that.’ And then also, it allows her to have a legacy in the future – she will grow this club to a point where she’s creating a pathway for the next young players to come through in London.”There are questions facing the club in relation to how much they have been spending and eyebrows were raised – to put it mildly – around the rest of the league when London City recorded an operating loss of more than 10 times their revenue for the 2024-25 season, when they won promotion as second-tier champions. Since then salary cap rules have been introduced in the WSL, stating no club’s player wage bill can exceed the following figures combined: 80% of revenue, plus up to £4m or a further 25% of revenue (whichever is higher).View image in fullscreenAlexia Putellas’s arrival has undoubtedly put London City Lionesses on the map.Photograph: Nina Farooqi/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockLast season, when London City finished sixth, the league’s handbook said no punishments would be dished out for any breaches of that cap for that campaign only. From this term, points deductions could apply, which is one reason why it was imperative to increase commercial revenues. But were they within the rules last term?skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“We are 100% within the rules, we will always be,” Semmens says. “It’s so important to Michele.” He says the “goal of the business” is to be profitable within five years and likens last year’s investments to a “start-up fund”: “The [salary cap] rules were set up with a clear understanding that they wouldn’t come until this year. The handbook is 100% clear. We want to see investment coming into the women’s game.
